author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A single-volume omnibus gathering five of PKD's central novels — including The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch and A Scanner Darkly — as a compact route into the reality-instability at the core of his work.
page_summary:
This is a collected omnibus edition, not a novel, binding five of Philip K. Dick's major works together in one volume — among them The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch, Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?, and A Scanner Darkly.

The grouping matters because it lines up, back to back, the books where PKD's signature preoccupations reach full pressure: manufactured realities and drug-induced worlds, the empathy test for the human, surveillance and the fracturing of the self. Read together, the novels show how consistently he returned to a single question — how do you know the world in front of you is real — and how many forms that question could take. Editions of this kind function as a canon-forming gesture, presenting a compact 'essential' Dick to new readers and libraries.
